buildTown.hint.housing: Homes attract new families. Free beds in the settlement: {n}.
buildTown.hint.road: Drag your finger across the map to draw a road. Buildings next to a road can be reached from home.
buildTown.hint.work: Work keeps adults busy and fills the storehouse. Out of work: {n}.
buildTown.hint.infra: Wells, lanterns, squares and storehouses make life better within their range.
buildTown.hint.service: Services run on staff – residents who can reach them will take the jobs.
buildTown.hint.farm: Farm buildings: animals, processing and watering.
buildTown.hint.deco: Decorations cheer up residents living within 3 tiles.
buildTown.drawMore: Drag across the map to draw the next stretch
buildTown.placeMore: Tap the map to place another
buildTown.effect.water: Homes within {r} tiles are cosier, and the well helps put out fires.
buildTown.effect.light: Safer streets after dark within {r} tiles.
buildTown.effect.school: Children learn and adults work 5% more efficiently.
buildTown.effect.clinic: Safety, quick care for animals and medicine made from herbs.
buildTown.effect.fire: Fewer fires, and any fire is out within an hour.
buildTown.effect.police: Safety and half as many quarrels between neighbours.
buildTown.effect.market: Residents buy food here – you earn from every meal.
buildTown.effect.storage: Adds {v} storage space to the settlement.
buildTown.effect.hall: Settlement council, specialisation and {v} more storage space.
buildTown.effect.transport: Commutes of up to {d} tiles without roads, +10% efficiency.
buildTown.effect.build: Builders speed up construction and repair damage.
buildTown.homeEmpty: The home awaits tenants. New families arrive at 9:00 when the settlement has food and a good mood.
buildTown.homeWaiting: Nobody can move in until the home is whole.
buildTown.vacancy: Open jobs: {n}. They go to unemployed residents who can get here – by road or within {d} tiles of home.
buildTown.noAccess: Nobody can get here: connect the building to homes by road or place it closer (within {d} tiles of home).
buildTown.noPeople: Open jobs: {n}. New residents will take them – build homes.
buildTown.storageFull: Storage is full (materials and goods) – production is waiting.
buildTown.limitReached: Enough in stock (up to {n}) – production is waiting.
buildTown.noFish: The fish aren't biting – the catch resumes at another time.
buildTown.autoNoStaff: Hire a crew and the machine will run on its own – from storage to storage.
buildTown.storageNote: Only materials and goods count – food takes no space.
buildTown.sickText: Sick animals give no produce. One medicine cures them at once (you have {n}). The clinic makes medicine from herbs.
site.noYard: Slower without a builders' yard – build one and hire builders.
site.noBuilders: The builders' yard is waiting for builders.
site.queued: In queue: {n}. Builders are finishing an earlier job.
site.buildersOff: Builders ({n}) return in the morning – construction is slower at night.
site.homeSoon: Once finished, up to {n} people can live here.
site.fireCrew: Firefighters are already putting it out.
site.fireAlone: The fire will burn out in a few hours. A fire station would put it out within an hour.
site.brokenText: The building has stopped. Builders will fix it in about 3 work-hours, or repair it now.
site.damagedText: The building won't work until it is repaired.
site.damagedHome: Nobody can live here until the home is repaired.
site.scratchedText: It still works, but a repair would help.
territory.title: Settlement land
territory.hint: Tap a plot along the border to buy it.
territory.hintNone: Explore the map around the settlement to buy another plot.
territory.hintTier: More land from the “{tier}” stage (up to {n} plots).
territory.hintMax: The settlement already has all the land it can hold.
territory.intro: Plots with a price tag can be added to the settlement.
territory.buyText: A new plot of land for {cost}. Settlement land: {n}/{limit}.
